Protect Your Bicycle: Choose Locks That Work Together

By Mrs. Shopper.

A strong lock is only one part of bicycle security. Use a hardened-steel chain or U-lock to secure the frame to a fixed rack, then add an alarm to make tampering easier to notice.

Start with the frame, not just a wheel

A bicycle is easier to take when the lock secures only a removable wheel or a light accessory. Choose a fixed, purpose-built rack and pass the main lock through the frame and a wheel where the rack allows it. Keep the lock off the ground when possible and leave as little free space inside it as practical.

Look beyond the word “heavy-duty.” Check the material, shackle or link thickness, locking mechanism, usable length, and whether the lock fits the rack and frame. A hardened-steel chain can wrap around awkward shapes. A rigid U-lock can leave less room for leverage when correctly fitted.

Use more than one kind of protection

A second lock with a different design can make a theft attempt take longer. An alarm adds a warning when a parked bicycle is moved or disturbed, but it does not physically secure the frame. Treat an alarm as an extra layer, not a substitute for a strong lock and a sound locking point.

Three parts of a stronger setup

Secure

Use a hardened-steel chain or U-lock around the frame and a fixed rack.

Reinforce

Add a second lock to cover a wheel or a part the main lock cannot reach.

Alert

Use a movement-sensitive alarm as a warning layer. It does not replace a lock.

Choose a secure locking point first. Then combine different lock types to cover the parts each one leaves exposed.

Compare the three security layers

Hardened-Steel Chain Lock

Best for: Wrapping around a frame and a wide rack.
